compiled_state.description:
## The failure

Three unrelated Gerrit changes (2648, 2652, 2656) all failed the `require resolvable rebar ticket`
job within minutes of each other on 2026-09-05, each in ~75 seconds. The failure is in the
**checkout step, before any patchset content is evaluated**:

```
git fetch https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar refs/changes/56/2656/1
error: RPC failed; HTTP 504 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 504
gerrit-checkout action  outcome=failure  duration_ms=61003
```

Because the step fails before reading anything from the change, no change can be responsible for
its own failure. Each got a `Verified -1`, which also INVALIDATES the work: a `-1` sends a change
back around the loop on an already-saturated queue.

## The mechanism (strong correlation + plausible cause; NOT yet proven)

Measured on the host at 03:20 UTC, minutes after the failures:

```
systemctl: rebar-autodeploy.service   loaded activating start   "reflect main on the box"
uptime:    load average: 2.87, 5.62, 7.57      <- 15-min load 7.57, 1-min already falling
docker ps: rebar-mcp-1518bb992384-8093   Up 4 minutes            <- freshly rebuilt+redeployed
GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/  ->  HTTP 200 in 0.26s <- Gerrit fine on light requests
free -m:   4204 MB available of 7813 (54%)                       <- NOT memory exhaustion
```

So: commit `1518bb992384` merged to `main`; `rebar-autodeploy` rebuilt and redeployed the MCP
container on the same host that serves Gerrit; the box carried a 15-minute load average of ~8;
Gerrit continued serving light HTTP fine but timed out at 60s on heavyweight `refs/changes/*`
fetches; CI's checkout step 504'd for every change unlucky enough to be in that window.

That gives a **self-inflicted feedback loop: merging a change degrades CI for the changes still in
flight.** The busier the pipeline, the more merges, the more autodeploys, the more spurious `-1`s —
and each `-1` puts another run back in the queue.

**Stated honestly:** this is a strong correlation with a coherent mechanism, not a proven cause. It
has NOT been reproduced deliberately. The proof would be to trigger an autodeploy while timing
`git fetch refs/changes/...` from off-box and show the latency crossing 60s, then show it does not
cross when the box is idle.

## Corroborating signal

`rebar/host:voter_errors` climbed across the same window — `1, 0, 0, 4, 1, 8` per 15-minute bucket,
and `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` is in ALARM. The component that casts votes on Gerrit is failing at
the same time as the component that fetches from Gerrit. One shared dependency, two symptoms.

## Why this deserves a fix rather than a standing `recheck` habit

Retrying is exactly the wrong reflex, and AGENTS.md says so: `recheck` is reserved for provably
environmental faults, and a flaky gate is a bug to root-cause. This one IS provably environmental
per-instance — but the environment is ours, the trigger is our own merge, and the frequency scales
with throughput. Left alone it trains everyone to retry, which is how a regression oracle stops
being one.

It also interacts with `witted-invisible-roan` (`9ea3-7d07`, MCP 502s after long gate jobs): same
box, same contention, different victim. They may share a root cause.

## Directions (none endorsed)

- Nice/ionice the autodeploy rebuild so it cannot outbid Gerrit for CPU and IO.
- Serialise autodeploy against in-flight CI, or defer it while change-ref fetches are being served.
- Give CI's checkout a retry with backoff on 5xx specifically (narrow, does not mask a real fault,
  but treats the symptom).
- Move the build off the Gerrit host entirely — the durable fix, and the largest.
- Right-size the instance; note memory was NOT the constraint here, so this is about CPU/IO.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The mechanism is PROVEN, not inferred: `refs/changes/*` fetch latency is measured from
      off-box during an autodeploy and while idle, and the difference is shown to cross CI's 60s
      ceiling. If the measurement refutes the autodeploy link, that is a valid outcome — record it
      and find the real trigger.
- [ ] A merge to `main` no longer causes an unrelated in-flight change to fail its checkout.
      Demonstrated by triggering the two concurrently after the fix.
- [ ] `voter_errors` returns to 0 across a normal merge, and `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` clears.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen, it does NOT take the form of "retry until green" alone. A retry may be
      part of the fix but must not be all of it; record why the chosen contention control is
      sufficient.
- [ ] The relationship to `9ea3-7d07` is settled explicitly: same root cause (then merge them) or
      different (then say how they differ).
compiled_state.title: A merge to main triggers an autodeploy that degrades Gerrit enough to 504 CI's change-ref checkout, failing unrelated in-flight changes: three Verified -1s in one window, all before any patchset content ran
